claim: Patchline sweeps a large public migration corpus with deterministic sharding and resumable progress so a thousand-repository run can be split across machines and restarted after interruption without reprocessing or dropping work. The worker assigns each repository to a shard with a pure content-derived hash so the assignment is identical on every run, and computes the remaining work as the corpus minus an already-completed checkpoint set. The gate proves the shard assignment is byte-identical across two independent runs, that every repository lands in exactly one of the requested shards, and that resuming from a checkpoint yields strictly fewer repositories that exclude the completed ones.
